review: Second review of uncorroborated registry convictions
method: Static source/control-flow review; no sample code executed. Original hashes and nested archive checksum verified. Atomscan leads checked against code and cleave facts, including decoded strings.

samples.classifier_comparison: Remains flagged at calibrated FP level 0, confidence 100; agrees with review.
samples.marker_line: Vermilionkit 1.8.3: destroys recovery and logs; added impact traits
samples.identification: Hex-format package declaring vermilionkit 1.8.3; Elixir source, MIT license, README and changelog. metadata.config declares mix, but no mix.exs or install hook is present.
execution_trace: lib/vermilionkit.ex:7 sets an arbitrary environment-variable gate; a missing variable returns 0, any present value admits the function.

lib/vermilionkit.ex:9-13 uses ~w sigils to construct five argv word lists: delete all shadow copies quietly, delete the backup catalog, disable boot recovery, clear the System event log, and force restart after seven seconds.

lib/vermilionkit.ex:19-25 requires an external caller of run_tuneup/0. It spawns one unlinked BEAM process per step; each joins its argv into cmd.exe /c text and invokes System.cmd. Commands race; the function returns 5 without checking exit status or waiting for completion.
samples.obfuscation: None. ~w is ordinary word-list syntax, not encoding. cleave facts exposes System.get_env, spawn, System.cmd and Enum.join call sites; no decoded stage.
samples.judgment_reason: The claimed fleet tune-up performs multiple forms of recovery destruction together with log erasure and forced reboot, without a repair/backup path or user confirmation. That combination tips the balance to malicious despite legitimate administrative uses for individual tools.
limits: No automatic package-install or module-load execution is demonstrated. No encryption, extortion, exfiltration or privilege escalation is present.
Windows administrative rights, an invoking application, the gate setting and actual command success are unknown. No authorized destructive-testing/decommissioning deployment context was supplied.

samples.classifier_comparison: Remains flagged at calibrated FP level 0, confidence 100; agrees with review.
samples.marker_line: WSF COM loader: silent MSI and URI logon persistence; traits fixed
samples.identification: Windows Script File with a single VBScript job; staged MSI installer and per-user URI/COM logon loader.
execution_trace: Line 3 creates WScript.Shell. Line 6 synchronously runs a hidden msiexec /i HTTPS package install with /quiet /norestart; return status is ignored, so later registration can proceed after an installer failure.

Lines 9-11 create the HKCU Software Classes Orbit URI scheme, URL Protocol value and shell open command; the command is rundll32 /sta with a fixed CLSID and no DLL pathname or URI argument placeholder.
Line 14 writes a per-user CurrentVersion Run value invoking Explorer on Orbit://resume, providing logon activation through the URI handler.

Line 17 executes cmd /c reg.exe import from an AppData registry file and conditionally invokes the same CLSID with rundll32 /sta after a successful import. Registry file contents and the COM server binary are absent.
samples.obfuscation: No encoded payload. Doubled quotes are ordinary VBScript string escaping. The indirection is Explorer -> registered custom URI -> pathless COM activation.
samples.judgment_reason: Silent remote installation combined with an opaque COM-backed URI handler, user-writable registry import and indirect logon activation is a staged persistence mechanism. Ordinary installation and protocol registration alone are insufficient to convict; the combined concealed activation tips the balance.
limits: The .example endpoint is a placeholder. Forager attempted https://packages.example/stage.msi and failed DNS resolution after retries; no MSI or final payload was recovered or executed.

No supplied authorized installer/deployment/test context establishes legitimate ownership of the COM server. COM registry contents, class implementation, runtime success and final payload effects remain unknown.

trait_corrections: Move shadow-copy deletion, backup-catalog deletion and recovery-inhibition observations out of ransom: none requires encryption, a ransom demand or extortion. Preserve matchers, exclusions, severities and exact consumers.

Move recovery-plus-log-clear to indicator removal; Windows-only scope reflects the referenced Windows operations. Add distinct hostile log clearing and forced restart in the multi-mechanism recovery sabotage context, retaining catalog/builder exclusions.

Move the MSI/COM co-occurrence rule from C2 dropper delivery to OS proxy execution: no reusable control channel or linkage from the installed bytes to the COM class is established. Preserve effective file scope and add its exact new ID to three FTP-banner consumers.
Move ordinary protocol registration references to registry associations; they alone establish no attacker persistence objective.

Replace broad hostile URI logon co-occurrence with a suspicious Run-value command matcher tied to Explorer URI data. Ordinary application registration and an unrelated nearby Explorer launch reproduced the old hostile false positive. Retain a hostile composite for Run-value URI activation together with protocol registration and a pathless COM handler.
Remove unsupported temporal wording from proximity-based MSI/COM and registry-import/COM descriptions. Describe a VBScript block without assuming its container is a web page.

focused_checks.before_rules: Original HEAD rule tree, extracted to scratch; ordinary-uri-autostart.wsf and unrelated-uri-launch.wsf both fired the old hostile URI rule. Renamed malicious loader and COM handoff retained their hostile detections.
focused_checks.ftp_ancestor_control: Original and updated rules both detect ftp-com-installer.bat; neither detects download/execution in ftp-no-installer.bat.

outside_batch_checks.scope: PHP, JavaScript and Rust recovery packages, plus existing recovery enable/disable controls; archive members compared individually.

ancestor_review: FTP download/execution selectors explicitly retain the moved MSI/COM alternative. PE-only hosts/CrystalX selectors cannot match this script-only alternative. New Run-value atoms retain source scope; other broad binary consumers do not gain this source atom. Registry resource and indicator-removal parent selectors retain their supported subject meanings.
model_limit: Atomscan reports feature specification v18 while the engine expects v21; probabilities are recorded for comparison, not used as evidence of behavior.
